summary:
FlameGuard AI is an interactive web-based research dashboard developed by Team Hustlers for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It helps researchers, students, and space enthusiasts explore, compare, and prioritize NASA's microgravity combustion investigations to better understand fire safety in space.

The platform features a searchable research catalog, side-by-side experiment comparisons, transparent relevance rankings, and a source-linked research assistant. By organizing NASA's combustion research into fire prevention, detection, and suppression categories, FlameGuard AI makes complex scientific information easier to access and understand.

Our goal is to support safer future spacecraft, lunar habitats, and Mars missions through accessible, evidence-linked research discovery.
details:
FlameGuard AI — Microgravity Fire Research Explorer

FlameGuard AI is an interactive web-based research prototype created by Team Hustlers for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the Flame in Freefall challenge.

What does our project do?

Our application helps researchers, students, and space enthusiasts explore NASA's microgravity combustion investigations. It organizes scientific research into three important fire-safety categories: prevention, detection, and suppression.

Key Features

  • Research Explorer: Search and filter 12 curated NASA combustion investigations.
  • Study Comparison: Compare experiments such as BASS and FLEX based on their objectives, fuels, experimental apparatus, and safety relevance.
  • Research Assistant: Retrieve relevant investigation summaries with links to NASA research sources.
  • Relevance Ranking: Prioritize investigations using transparent, heuristic discovery scores.
  • Source Transparency: Provide references to NASA resources and explain scientific limitations.

Technology

The prototype uses HTML, CSS, and JavaScript and runs locally in a modern web browser without requiring a backend server.

Creativity and Impact

FlameGuard AI makes complex space combustion research easier to navigate and compare. It aims to support early-stage research discovery for spacecraft, lunar habitats, and future Mars exploration.

Scientific Limitations

The current prototype uses curated research descriptions rather than raw experimental measurements. Its assistant uses keyword-based retrieval rather than a generative AI model. Relevance scores are not fire-risk probabilities, and the application does not provide validated scientific predictions.

Our future goal is to incorporate structured NASA PSI experimental data and develop more advanced, evidence-grounded analysis tools.
